bull.b: Consistent multi-year revenue growth alongside expanding gross, operating, and net margins indicates operating leverage and improving business quality. This supports durable earnings growth as Boston Scientific scales its broad medical-device portfolio.

Robust free cash flow gives Boston Scientific capacity to fund product development, strategic investments, acquisitions, and restructuring while supporting financial flexibility. The scale of cash generation strengthens the company’s ability to compound its device ecosystem.

Double-digit growth across several franchises, new FDA clearances, and investments in adjacent technologies diversify growth beyond individual products. This broad pipeline can improve market position and sustain procedure-driven demand over multiple years.

bear.b: Clinical evidence has changed referral patterns, while stand-alone procedures declined low-teens year over year. Management does not assume recovery in 2027, creating a durable risk to growth, mix, and utilization of a key franchise.

Competitive share loss in U.S. electrophysiology and weakness in cardiac rhythm management expose portfolio gaps in important categories. Prolonged pressure could constrain revenue growth, reduce operating leverage, and require heavier investment to regain position.

The global systems disruption can affect order fulfillment, customer service, manufacturing coordination, and near-term cash conversion. Uncertainty over restoration timing and financial impact makes this an operational risk that could persist beyond the initial disclosure.
